xia-chao opened issue #15112:

wasmtime serve -W timeout=0 or --post-return-timeout 0 burns 100-220% CPU (same server without the flag: ~5%). A zero timeout makes the epoch interval zero (serve.rs:746), so EpochThread loops on sleep(0) (serve.rs:1263).

Reject zero and sub-millisecond values, clamp the thread interval, or document 0 as "time out immediately"?

Repro: wasmtime serve -Scli --post-return-timeout 0 <component>, then ps -o %CPU -p <pid>.

alexcrichton commented on issue #15112:

Subjectively I think this is fine, it's a user-supplied parameter and you're getting what you configured. It's a bit odd but it feels a bit too niche to try and rule out.

pchickey commented on issue #15112:

I would accept a patch that adds a clap value parser to reject zero values for those - a NonZeroDurationParser built in this style, for type Value = Duration; and excluding the case equal to Duration::new(0,0)

pchickey edited a comment on issue #15112:

I would accept a patch that adds a clap value parser to reject zero values for those - a NonZeroDurationParser built in this style, for type Value = Duration; and rejecting the case equal to Duration::new(0,0).

pchickey edited a comment on issue #15112:

I would accept a patch that adds a clap value parser to reject zero values for those - a NonZeroDurationParser built in this style, for type Value = Duration; and rejecting the case equal to Duration::new(0,0).

To me this is a usability hint and not a correctness issue - as Alex says, you're getting what you configured, but some configurations don't make sense and we could tell the user that in the cli. In the API, the user gets what they asked for.
